summary: This is a careful, well‑executed preregistered paired, emulation‑grounded experiment comparing a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline against an LLM‑only pipeline. Execution, logging, and archival artifacts are complete and consistent with the preregistration. The confirmatory outcome is a valid null result (no unsafe applies observed under either arm), and the manuscript appropriately interprets that null under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics. Major strengths: rigorous preregistration, full archival of traces and hashes (including the required master_prompt locator), and transparent accounting. Remaining problems are manuscript‑level and resolvable from the archived artifacts.
critical_issues: References section uses identifier URLs (arXiv/DOI) rather than a conventional IEEE‑style bibliographic list with full metadata; the paper must provide standard numbered IEEE bibliography entries so each cited record can be checked to support the proximate claim.

The Disclosure Statement in the manuscript duplicates run‑level provenance and internal artifact paths/hashes beyond the one mandatory master_prompt locator and is not concise as required by the track guidance. It must be condensed in the paper (keeping exactly the one required master_prompt locator+SHA‑256) and move additional run‑level hashes/paths to the archived execution manifest referenced in the Disclosure Statement.
required_revisions: Replace the current reference list with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography containing full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year, and stable identifier) for every cited source. Ensure each numbered citation in text maps correctly to the IEEE entry and that each cited source actually supports the adjacent claim (use the archived verified bibliography to populate entries).

Condense the Disclosure Statement in the manuscript to a concise paragraph that includes: (a) LLM identifier(s) used, (b) the registered adapter/orchestration names, (c) the exact immutable initial master prompt locator and its single SHA‑256 digest (the mandatory pair), (d) a concise statement of human vs post‑lock autonomy, and (e) a pointer to the archived execution manifest that contains detailed per‑call traces, artifact hashes, and full provenance. Remove routine internal paths/hashes and per‑file SHA lists from the manuscript body (these may remain in the archived bundle referenced).

Add one clear, explicit sentence in Methods or Results referencing the archived sensitivity analyses and deterministic reconciliation artifacts to state that the preregistered sensitivity treatments (possible false‑safe inclusion and failure‑as‑unsafe) were executed per plan and that no exclusions/flags occurred (point to deterministic_reconciliation.json and analysis artifacts). This makes explicit that the primary analysis exclusions were considered and that none affected outcomes.
optional_revisions: Add one brief explanatory sentence clarifying why the paired bootstrap CI is degenerate ([0.00,0.00]) and why the exact McNemar test is uninformative when n10=n01=0, cross‑referencing the archived paired_contingency_table.csv for transparency.

In Related Work or Discussion, convert any remaining identifier‑only references in prose to IEEE numbered citations and, if space permits, add one short sentence contrasting this null outcome with published NetConfArena‑style baseline unsafe rates (with an IEEE citation) to better contextualize external baseline expectations.

Move Figure/Table captions closer to their referenced artifacts and (optionally) include the path to the archived figure/table artifact in the execution bundle (not in the main text) to simplify reviewer verification.
